text:
### Escalation  
**Incident Escalation Triggers:**  
| Loss Amount | Escalation | Timeline |
|-------------|-----------|----------|
| <£1k | Department Manager | Report to Risk |
| £1k–£10k | Risk Manager | Report to CRO within 1 day |
| £10k–£100k | CRO + CEO | Report within 24 hours |
| >£100k | Board + Regulators | Immediate + regulatory notification |

raw_entities.name: Incident Escalation Policy
raw_entities.description: A policy governing the escalation of financial incidents based on loss amount thresholds, defining reporting timelines and responsible parties at each escalation level. The policy establishes mandatory escalation triggers ranging from departmental reporting for losses under £1,000 to immediate board and regulatory notification for losses exceeding £100,000.

raw_entities.name: Escalation to Department Manager for Losses Under £1,000
raw_entities.description: Incidents resulting in losses below £1,000 must be escalated to the Department Manager with a report to Risk. This represents the lowest escalation threshold in the incident management framework.

raw_entities.name: Escalation to Risk Manager for Losses Between £1,000 and £10,000
raw_entities.description: Incidents resulting in losses between £1,000 and £10,000 must be escalated to the Risk Manager with a report to the Chief Risk Officer within one business day.
context: £1k–£10k | Risk Manager | Report to CRO within 1 day

raw_entities.name: Escalation to CRO and CEO for Losses Between £10,000 and £100,000
raw_entities.description: Incidents resulting in losses between £10,000 and £100,000 must be escalated to both the Chief Risk Officer and Chief Executive Officer with a mandatory reporting timeline of 24 hours.

raw_entities.name: Escalation to Board and Regulators for Losses Exceeding £100,000
raw_entities.description: Incidents resulting in losses exceeding £100,000 must be escalated immediately to the Board and relevant regulators with concurrent regulatory notification. This represents the highest escalation level requiring immediate action.

raw_entities.name: Department Manager
raw_entities.description: The Department Manager is responsible for receiving and handling incident escalations for losses below £1,000, with an obligation to report to Risk.

raw_entities.name: Risk Manager
raw_entities.description: The Risk Manager is responsible for receiving incident escalations for losses between £1,000 and £10,000 and ensuring reporting to the Chief Risk Officer within one business day.
context: £1k–£10k | Risk Manager | Report to CRO within 1 day

raw_entities.name: Chief Risk Officer
raw_entities.description: The Chief Risk Officer is responsible for receiving incident escalations for losses between £1,000 and £10,000 (within 1 day) and for losses between £10,000 and £100,000 (within 24 hours), and must escalate to the CEO and Board respectively.
context: £1k–£10k | Risk Manager | Report to CRO within 1 day

raw_entities.name: Chief Executive Officer
raw_entities.description: The Chief Executive Officer is responsible for receiving incident escalations for losses between £10,000 and £100,000 within 24 hours and for losses exceeding £100,000 with immediate notification.

raw_entities.name: Board
raw_entities.description: The Board is responsible for receiving immediate notification of incidents resulting in losses exceeding £100,000 and for coordinating regulatory notification.

raw_entities.name: Financial Loss
raw_entities.description: Financial loss resulting from incidents is the primary risk category addressed by this escalation policy. The policy categorises risk severity by loss amount thresholds, triggering proportionate escalation and reporting obligations.
